overview.headline: DNA bases, double helix structure and copying in cells

keyPoints.point: Students learn that DNA is the hereditary material in humans and other organisms.
keyPoints.quote: DNA, or deoxyribonucleic acid, is the hereditary material in humans and almost all other organisms.

keyPoints.point: Students learn that human DNA consists of about 3 billion bases that are largely the same in all people.
keyPoints.quote: Human DNA consists of about 3 billion bases, and more than 99 percent of those bases are the same in all people.

keyPoints.point: Students learn that DNA bases pair up to form base pairs as A with T and C with G.
keyPoints.quote: DNA bases pair up with each other, A with T and C with G, to form units called base pairs.

keyPoints.point: Students learn that each strand of DNA can serve as a pattern for duplicating the sequence of bases.
keyPoints.quote: Each strand of DNA in the double helix can serve as a pattern for duplicating the sequence of bases.

keyTerms.gloss: Material in cells that carries hereditary instructions for building organisms
keyTerms.quote: DNA, or deoxyribonucleic acid, is the hereditary material in humans and almost all other organisms.

keyTerms.gloss: DNA located in the cell nucleus
keyTerms.quote: Most DNA is located in the cell nucleus (where it is called nuclear DNA)

keyTerms.gloss: Small amount of DNA found in mitochondria that converts energy from food
keyTerms.quote: but a small amount of DNA can also be found in the mitochondria (where it is called mitochondrial DNA or mtDNA)

keyTerms.gloss: Chemical base that pairs with thymine in the DNA code
keyTerms.quote: The information in DNA is stored as a code made up of four chemical bases: adenine (A), guanine (G), cytosine (C), and thymine (T).

keyTerms.gloss: Units formed by paired bases across the ladder rungs
keyTerms.quote: DNA bases pair up with each other, A with T and C with G, to form units called base pairs.

keyTerms.gloss: Base joined to sugar and phosphate in a DNA strand
keyTerms.quote: Together, a base, sugar, and phosphate are called a nucleotide.

keyTerms.gloss: Spiral shape made by two long strands of nucleotides
keyTerms.quote: Nucleotides are arranged in two long strands that form a spiral called a double helix.
